_comment: Traditional dishes. destinationId is where to try it; businessId is set only where a participating partner actually serves it — most do not yet, and that is shown honestly rather than invented.

name: Eromba
description: Boiled and mashed vegetables — commonly potato, and whatever greens are in season — pounded together with ngari (fermented fish) and chillies. The everyday comfort dish of the Manipur valley, eaten with steamed rice.
story: Made at home most days rather than for show; a household's eromba is a matter of personal taste in how much ngari and chilli goes in.

name: Chak-hao Kheer
description: A pudding made from chak-hao, the aromatic black rice grown in Manipur, simmered slowly in milk until it turns a deep purple, and sweetened.
story: Chak-hao is grown mainly for festive and ceremonial cooking rather than as a daily staple grain.

name: Singju
description: A tossed salad of thinly sliced raw or lightly blanched vegetables — banana flower, cabbage or seasonal greens — with roasted gram powder, perilla seeds and a dash of ngari.
story: Sold by the stallholders of Ima Keithel, made to order while you wait.

name: Kangshoi
description: A light, mostly clear vegetable stew — seasonal greens, pumpkin or beans simmered in water with a little ngari — that sits alongside a Manipuri meal the way a dal or a broth would elsewhere.

name: Nga Thongba
description: Fish — often drawn from Loktak Lake — cooked down with onions, ginger and mustard oil into a thick, dark curry.
story: No partner around Loktak serves this on the platform yet; it is listed because it is real and worth knowing about before you get there.

name: Morok Metpa
description: A pounded chutney of roasted or boiled tomato, chillies and a little ngari, served in a small heap beside the rice rather than mixed through it.

name: Hawaijar
description: Soybeans fermented over several days until sticky and pungent, then used as a strong-flavoured base stirred into a vegetable dish rather than eaten on its own.
story: An acquired taste for a first-time visitor; a small amount goes a long way in the dish it flavours.

name: Utti
description: Black gram, often mixed with rice, soaked and cooked soft, then finished with a little oil and seasoning. A common breakfast plate around the market in the early morning.

name: Chagempomba
description: Chayote (a pale, mild squash grown widely in the valley) grated and cooked with rice flour and sugar into a dense, lightly sweet dessert, finished with sesame.

name: Bamboo Shoot with Smoked Pork
description: A hill preparation from the Tangkhul households around Ukhrul: smoked pork simmered slowly with fermented or fresh bamboo shoot, ginger and local herbs, distinct in style from the valley's fish-based cooking.
story: No partner around Ukhrul serves this on the platform yet.

name: Fermented Bamboo Shoot Pickle
description: Bamboo shoot fermented, then pickled with chillies and mustard oil — a sharp, sour condiment served in small amounts alongside a hill meal.
